CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

Overview

n1qn1 (repository n1qn1c) is an R port of the Scilab n1qn1 module: unconstrained quasi-Newton BFGS optimization that can take a user-supplied (compressed) starting Hessian. The numerical core is C code produced by f2c from the Scilab Fortran and then hand-edited, so the package has no Fortran sources. A thin C++/RcppArmadillo layer connects R (or compiled) objective/gradient functions to the C core. It is used by nlmixr2est, which links to it through a function-pointer table (see below).

  • License: CeCILL-2 (LICENCE, inst/COPYING)
  • Imports: Rcpp; LinkingTo: Rcpp, RcppArmadillo
  • Exports only n1qn1() and .n1qn1ptr()
  • testthat edition 3, roxygen2 8.1.0

Architecture

Call path

  1. n1qn1() (R/n1qn1.R) coerces arguments to integer/double, computes nzm = ceiling(n * (n + 13) / 2), picks mode (1 = no Hessian, 2 = zm supplied, 3 = restart=TRUE), checks the length of zm, then calls .Call(n1qn1_wrap, ...) (13 args).
  2. n1qn1_wrap() (src/RcppExpMod.cpp) validates n/nzm (including an n * (n + 1) int overflow guard) BEFORE allocating, wraps the objective/gradient in Rcpp::EvalStandard (R function) or Rcpp::EvalCompiled (external pointer) from src/evaluate.h, and passes the static callback fwrap() to the C core.
  3. n1qn1_() / n1qn1a_() / majour_() (src/n1qn1_all.c) run the BFGS iterations; helpers ajour_, calmaj_, proj_, satur_ live in their own f2c-translated files.
  4. On return, the LDL’ factor in zm is converted to the full Hessian H and its lower triangle c.hess with Armadillo. The result list is value, par, H, c.hess, n.fn, n.gr. With assign=TRUE the R wrapper stores c.hess in environment.

Thread safety

Per-call state in src/RcppExpMod.cpp (fev, gev, call counters, print flag) is thread_local, and static locals were removed from the translated C code. Do not reintroduce file-level mutable globals or static locals in src/*.c. EvalBase has a virtual destructor because callbacks are deleted through a base pointer – keep it.

Function-pointer API for downstream packages

_n1qn1_ptr() in src/init.c (R: .n1qn1ptr()) returns a named list of external pointers: index 0 n1qn1F, 1 n1qn1F2, 2 n1qn1_. inst/include/n1qn1c.h declares the matching typedefs, the iniN1qn1c macro and iniN1qn1cPtrs0(), which installs the pointers in a downstream package (this lets nlmixr2est avoid ABI coupling and re-submission when n1qn1 changes). The same three functions are also registered with R_RegisterCCallable.

  • Treat the table as APPEND-ONLY: never reorder, rename, remove, or change the signature of an existing slot; add new entries at the end and bump nVec plus the header together.
  • Changing inst/include/n1qn1c.h affects packages compiled against it; do not change existing typedefs.

.Call registration

src/init.c hand-maintains R_init_n1qn1 and the callMethods[] table with hardcoded argument counts (_n1qn1_ptr 0, n1qn1_wrap 13). There is no RcppExports.cpp. If you change the arguments of n1qn1_wrap, update the extern prototype and the count in src/init.c as well, or the call fails at runtime with an argument-count error.

Build configuration

src/Makevars and src/Makevars.win list sources explicitly (SOURCES_C, SOURCES_CPP) and link $(LAPACK_LIBS) $(BLAS_LIBS) $(FLIBS). A new source file must be added to BOTH files.

Important Files

File Purpose
R/n1qn1.R n1qn1() R wrapper and .n1qn1ptr()
src/RcppExpMod.cpp n1qn1_wrap .Call entry, fwrap callback, Hessian reconstruction
src/evaluate.h EvalBase/EvalStandard/EvalCompiled callback classes
src/n1qn1_all.c f2c-translated n1qn1_, n1qn1a_, majour_
src/ajour.c, calmaj.c, proj.c, satur.c f2c-translated helper routines
src/n1qn1.h S_fp/S2_fp/U_fp callback typedefs
src/init.c Routine registration, CCallables, pointer table
inst/include/n1qn1c.h Public header for function-pointer linking

Testing

  • Tests live in tests/testthat/test-*.R: test-banana.R (Rosenbrock reference), test-coverage.R (print/invisible paths, EvalCompiled via XPtr), test-edge-cases.R, test-memory-safety.R.
  • test-memory-safety.R is excluded from the built tarball via .Rbuildignore (CRAN sanitizer machines flag its deliberate integer overflow). It still runs under devtools::test(). Do not remove that exclusion; keep overflow/large-n tests out of what CRAN runs.
  • The Rosenbrock example in the n1qn1() docs is the canonical reference problem; reuse it for new tests.
  • Assert on results (par, value, error messages), not on exact function-evaluation counts unless the existing tests already do.

CI

.github/workflows/: R-CMD-check.yaml, test-coverage.yaml (codecov), pkgdown.yaml (site at https://nlmixr2.github.io/n1qn1c/), and rhub.yaml (R-hub checks, e.g. sanitizer and valgrind platforms).

Code Style

R

  • Keep the public interface of n1qn1() stable; its argument names (call_eval, call_grad, max_iterations, print.functions, …) and return-list names (c.hess, n.fn, n.gr) are relied on by downstream code.
  • Internal helpers: .camelCase with a leading dot.
  • Never use pkg:::fun; tests already run in the package namespace.

C/C++

  • The f2c-derived C files are not idiomatic C; make minimal, targeted edits and keep the Fortran calling convention (int * arguments for Fortran INTEGER).
  • Validate inputs before any new/allocation in n1qn1_wrap, since Rf_error longjmps and would leak earlier allocations.
  • Use strict prototypes (CRAN requirement).
  • Printing must go through Rprintf, never printf/stdout.

Documentation and text

  • ASCII only everywhere (CRAN): use --, ->, straight quotes.
  • NEWS.md uses one # n1qn1 X.Y.Z-N heading per version with short bullet entries; add a bullet for user-visible changes.

Release / CRAN Cautions

  • nlmixr2est depends on this package; any change to the pointer table, n1qn1c.h, or the n1qn1() return value can break it on CRAN.
  • Check with sanitizers (gcc-ASAN, valgrind) before submission; CRAN has requested these for this package.
  • Do not add tests or examples that are slow, overflow integers, or depend on timing.

CRAN tests: never assert on timing

  • Never put a wall-clock timing expectation in a test that can run on CRAN: no expect_lt()/expect_true() on Sys.time() differences, system.time(), proc.time(), bench/microbenchmark results, or any other elapsed-time threshold. CRAN check machines are shared and heavily loaded, so elapsed time there is random and a timing assertion fails at random. Example: nlmixr2plot test-model-diagram.R asserted a modelGraph() call took < 30 s; on CRAN it took 48.4 s and failed.
  • Test the result, not the speed. If a speed regression guard is really needed, put it only in a test that starts with skip_on_cran() (or the package’s own CRAN skip helper), and never in examples or vignettes.
  • Tests that take more than a few seconds should also skip on CRAN.
